title: US officials say string of November outages was not a cyberattack, Hankook Ilbo reports
date_note: Date of the officials' statements per Hankook Ilbo (published 19 Nov); the outages it lists run 12 to 17 November.
summary: Hankook Ilbo lists outages from 12 to 17 November at Outlook and Teams, an FAA communications system, United Airlines, JPMorgan Chase, Apple and an NSA internal network. It reports DNI director Jay Clayton blamed maintenance and technical changes. AZ Free News quotes Clayton at a House hearing: "no evidence that this is a coordinated cyberattack or state-sponsored activity." El Financiero (EFE) reports Trump called them "todos sucesos independientes", not a coordinated cyberattack.
plain: A Korean newspaper reports that US officials say a run of outages at several big services was caused by individual technical problems, not a cyberattack.
exec: US officials link some outages to rushed patching of newly found flaws, per one report; a cyberattack is not fully ruled out by a quoted former analyst.
impact: Outages named by the article: Outlook and Teams, FAA communications, United Airlines, JPMorgan Chase, Apple services, an NSA internal network.

validation.note: Hankook Ilbo (relaying ABC) and AZ Free News (House Homeland Security hearing coverage) each report DNI Clayton saying there is no evidence of a coordinated or state-sponsored attack. Statements are as reported; hearing page not read. El Financiero (EFE, 20 Nov) reports Trump calling the outages independent events, not a coordinated attack.

review.note: Compared title, date (18 Nov hearing), outage list and dates, Clayton maintenance statement and quote against Hankook Ilbo and AZ Free News; category outage, not called an attack; corroboration and wording hold
